ui.prSub: Like a restaurant kitchen: the long cooking happens once, the protein is portioned, the vegetables are cut, the sauces and bases are made. Each day only the last bit of cooking is left, and no lunch should take more than 20 minutes.
ui.prHoras: Plan on about {h} hours on Sunday, with the stove, the oven and the cutting board working at the same time.
ui.prEstLargo: 1 · The long cooks: stove and oven first
ui.prR1: Everything cooked cools uncovered and is covered once cold. Into the fridge within two hours.
ui.prR2: Tape a label on every container: what it is and which day it is for. In a restaurant nothing goes into the fridge unlabeled.
ui.prR3: Frozen items move to the fridge the night before; never thaw on the counter.
ui.prR4: Raw on the bottom shelf, cooked on top: that way nothing drips onto what is ready to eat.
ui.prMieSub: Fresh produce for Thursday on gets cut midweek: cut on Sunday, it is tired by Friday.
ui.prChip: Prep plan · {n} min on the day
ui.prGCongela: freeze it; to the fridge on {d} night
ui.prOlla: Cook it all the way, as the recipe says. Cool uncovered, portion into one-day containers and cover once cold. Stews, soups and braises are better the next day.
ui.prOllaFideo: Do not cook the {x} in the pot: in the fridge they drink the broth and turn to mush. Cook them separately on the day.
ui.prOllaMar: Make the whole base (sofrito, stock or sauce) WITHOUT the {x}. Reheated fish and seafood dry out and turn rubbery: they go raw into the hot base on the day.
ui.prArroz: Cook it all the way. Spread it on a tray so it cools fast and portion it: rice is the one lunchbox item that can really make you sick if left warm.
ui.prArrozMar: Make the mother sauce or sofrito with the stock and par-cook the rice in it two-thirds of the time, still firm at the center. Spread on a tray and cool fast. The seafood ({x}) is portioned raw and goes in on the day.
ui.prRisotto: Par-cook the rice: sofrito, toast and stock for 12 minutes, still firm at the center. Spread it on a tray and cool fast. It is how restaurants serve risotto in 8 minutes.
ui.prHorno: Assemble in individual oven-safe dishes, bake it all the way, cool and cover. Portioned before baking, it cuts clean and reheats evenly.
ui.prPostre: Make it in full and portion it into one-day cups or containers.
ui.prPastaSalsa: Make the full sauce from the recipe, without the pasta, and portion it by day. The pasta gets par-cooked separately (below).
ui.prPasta: Cook it two minutes short of the package time, shock it in ice water, drain, toss with a little oil and portion into bags: it keeps three days. That is how pasta restaurants work.
ui.prPastaRellena: Shape them and lay them apart on a floured tray; freeze two hours and bag them. They cook from frozen. The sauce, made and portioned.
ui.prFideoArroz: Soak them in cold water the night before you eat them, drain and keep covered in the fridge: on the day they just finish in the pan.
ui.prArrozFrio: Cook it Sunday and store it spread out: fried rice needs cold, dry rice; freshly cooked rice sticks and turns to paste.
ui.prGrano: Cook it and cool it spread out; keep a little of its liquid so it does not dry out.
ui.prPapaFrita: Cut into sticks, par-cook 4 minutes in salted water (or 5 minutes in oil at 140 °C without browning), dry, freeze on a tray and bag. On the day it goes straight into hot oil or the air fryer: that is how restaurants do fries.
ui.prPapaCocida: Boil it in its skin until a knife goes in, not further, and cool uncovered. Do not freeze: it turns grainy.
ui.prPapaCriolla: Boil in its skin 12 minutes and cool: on the day it just browns in the pan.
ui.prYuca: Boil until it splits, remove the woody core and freeze in pieces: on the day it is fried or browned from frozen.
ui.prPatacon: First fry and smash on Sunday; freeze the patacones separated with paper. On the day, a three-minute second fry.
ui.prProtWok: Cut into even strips, marinate with the salty part of the recipe and a teaspoon of cornstarch (for chicken or beef it is velveting, which keeps it juicy) and portion by day.
ui.prProtWokMar: Peel or clean, pat dry and portion by day. Seafood marinades are short: add it on the day, ten minutes before.
ui.prProtPlancha: Portion ({g} g per serving), even out the thickness and season or marinate as the recipe says. In a flat bag with the air pressed out.
ui.prProtApana: Cut, season and bread completely. Freeze the pieces apart on a tray for two hours, then bag them: they fry from frozen and the crust gets crispier.
ui.prProtPrecuece: Pre-cook until done inside (steamed, simmered or baked, as the recipe asks) and cool. On the day it only gets browned: the crust takes minutes and the center is already done.
ui.prProtAsado: Cook it through on Sunday (oven or grill) and let it rest; large pieces get sliced. Store with its juices or glaze.
ui.prProtPescado: Clean, portion, pat dry and season. Whatever is not eaten Monday goes into the freezer as soon as you get home.
ui.prProtCrudo: Anything eaten raw is bought very fresh for that day or factory-frozen, and kept in the coldest part of the fridge.
ui.prProtTocino: Cut and brown it on Sunday; on the day it reheats in seconds.
ui.prDPlanchaSin: On the griddle or grill as the recipe says, with everything ready: {m} minutes.
ui.prPica: Cut them as the recipe asks and portion by day, in containers lined with a paper towel: they keep four days.
ui.prBlanq: Blanch two minutes in boiling salted water, shock in ice water, dry and freeze in portions: on the day they go straight into the pan.
ui.prHojas: Wash, dry thoroughly and store with paper towel: they last five days. Cut or tear them on the day.
ui.prHierba: Wash, dry and store wrapped in damp paper inside a bag: chop them on the day, chopped ahead they blacken.
ui.prAjo: Peeled, chopped garlic covered in oil, in a jar in the fridge: use it within four days. For longer, freeze it in ice cube trays.
ui.prFrascoWok: Mix the dish sauce in a jar: {x}. Shake before using; it keeps all week.
ui.prFrascoAlino: Make the dressing in a jar ({x}). Keep it separate until you eat.
ui.prMasaForma: Make the dough and filling, shape the pieces and freeze them raw, apart on a tray; then bag them. They cook from frozen.
ui.prMasaCocida: Cook them through, cool and freeze one by one: reheat steamed or covered in the microwave.
ui.prMasaPan: Bake it on Sunday, slice and freeze: slices go straight to the toaster.
ui.prMasaPlancha: Cook them all, separate with paper and freeze: reheat in a pan or toaster.
ui.prMasaPizza: Make the dough, stretch it and pre-bake the bases five minutes; cool and freeze. The toppings, cut and in containers.
ui.prTortilla: Confit the potatoes and onion in the oil as the recipe says, drain and refrigerate: on the day you just set the tortilla.
ui.prHuevoSofrito: Have the sofrito or the vegetables from the recipe cooked and cold: the eggs are made on the day.
ui.prEnsaladaComp: Cook the components ({x}) and chill them separately.
ui.prCrudoBase: Have the base ready without lime (chili, garlic and whatever is blended in), the cooked sides and the sliced onion in ice water, which keeps two days. Squeeze the lime on the day: squeezed ahead it turns bitter.
ui.prOjoCrudo: Careful: raw seafood does not travel in a lunchbox without cold. If you take it, use an insulated cooler with ice and eat it within two hours.
ui.prDRegen: Reheat the portion covered over low heat with two tablespoons of water or stock until it bubbles in the middle (or microwave three minutes, stirring halfway).
ui.prDFideo: Cook the {x} separately in salted water and add them to the hot dish.
ui.prDOllaMar: Bring the base to a boil, lower the heat and cook the {x} in it for {m} minutes, without a hard boil.
ui.prDArroz: Reheat the rice covered with three tablespoons of stock or water over low heat until it steams evenly.
ui.prDArrozMar: Sauté the {x} two minutes, add the par-cooked rice with a ladle of hot stock and finish six minutes, stirring.
ui.prDRisotto: Finish the rice with hot stock, a ladle at a time, six or seven minutes; off the heat, the butter and cheese.
ui.prDHorno: Oven or air fryer at 180 °C, covered, 12 minutes; uncover the last three to brown (or microwave four minutes).
ui.prDAsado: Reheat on a very hot griddle or in the air fryer, with some of its juices or glaze, until browned outside: six minutes.
ui.prDHornoMar: Bake the fish with its sides at 200 °C, {m} minutes, or en papillote.
ui.prDPostre: Done: just take it out of the fridge.
ui.prDMasaVapor: Steam them 15 minutes, or microwave covered four minutes.
ui.prDMasaPlancha: Warm them in a pan or toaster, one minute per side.
ui.prDMasaArepa: Cook them from frozen in a pan or griddle over medium heat, about six minutes per side.
ui.prDMasaFrita: Fry from frozen at 170 °C until golden, about 8 minutes (or air fryer at 190 °C, 12).
ui.prDMasaPan: Toast the slice straight from the freezer.
ui.prDMasaHorno: Bake from frozen at 190 °C until golden, about 15 minutes (or air fryer, 10).
ui.prDPizza: Top the pre-baked base and bake as hot as your oven goes, 10 minutes.
ui.prDArma: Warm the base in a pan, add the ready fillings and brown a couple of minutes.
ui.prDPasta: Bring water to a boil; dip the par-cooked pasta 60 seconds and finish two minutes in the pan with the hot sauce and a splash of the water.
ui.prDPastaEmul: Dip the par-cooked pasta 60 seconds in boiling water and make the sauce in the pan as the recipe says: the emulsion cannot be made ahead, but with everything ready it takes minutes.
ui.prDPastaRellena: Cook from frozen in boiling salted water four or five minutes, and toss with the hot sauce.
ui.prDWok: Wok or pan smoking hot: the protein in batches ({m} min), the pre-cut vegetables, the sauce from the jar and the starch. In order and without stopping.
ui.prDWokSin: A very hot pan or wok: what is already cooked and cut goes in by order, firmest first, tossed without stopping until it takes some color.
ui.prDPlancha: Take the {x} out ten minutes ahead, pat dry and sear in a very hot pan: {m} minutes total. Rest three while you warm the sides.
ui.prDFrito: Fry from frozen at 170 °C, {m} minutes (or air fryer at 200 °C, {m2}), and drain on a rack.
ui.prDFritoDora: Brown the pre-cooked protein in very hot oil or the air fryer, {m} minutes, until crusty.
ui.prDFritoMar: Pat dry, dredge in flour and fry, {m} minutes in total.
ui.prDFritoVeg: Fry or brown what you par-cooked, from frozen, until crisp.
ui.prDHuevo: The eggs, made fresh as the recipe says: {m} minutes.
ui.prDTortilla: Beat the eggs, mix in the confit potatoes, rest five minutes and set the tortilla: about eight minutes.
ui.prDMonta: Assemble with what is ready; the dressing stays separate until you eat.
ui.prDCrudo: Cut the fish or seafood, toss with the base, salt and freshly squeezed lime for two minutes, and serve.
ui.prDSushi: Sushi rice cannot be refrigerated because it hardens. Set the rice cooker timer the night before so it is ready; on the day you just season it and roll with what is already cut: fifteen minutes.
ui.prDRapido: It is a quick dish: with everything cut and measured since Sunday, make it as the recipe says, {m} minutes.
ui.prDPapaFrita: Fries: straight from the freezer into hot oil or the air fryer, 6 to 8 minutes, while the rest cooks.
ui.prDPatacon: Second fry for the patacones, three minutes, while the rest cooks.
ui.prDYuca: Fry or brown the cassava from frozen, seven minutes, while the rest cooks.
ui.prBase: Make it in full and store it: three days in the fridge, or frozen in portions.
ui.prDBase: It is ready to use in whatever calls for it.
ui.prPostreFrito: Make the dough and shape the pieces; freeze them raw, apart on a tray. The syrup or honey, made and jarred.
ui.prDPostreFrito: Fry from frozen until golden and coat with the warm syrup: about ten minutes.
ui.prCannoli: Fry the shells on Sunday and keep them in a dry jar; the filling, made and in the fridge.
ui.prDCannoli: Fill them right before eating: filled ahead, the shell softens within an hour.
ui.prTortaD: Shape the patties as the recipe says, with the potato or legumes already cooked, and freeze them raw, separated with paper.
ui.prEPailaD: Blend and strain the fruit base with the sugar and freeze it in flat portions.
ui.prEPailaA: With the base half-thawed, make it in the pan over salted ice, scraping without stopping: fifteen minutes, eaten right away.
ui.prChoclo: Cook it and cut off the kernels or slice into rounds: it keeps three days in the fridge and freezes well.
ui.prProtVivo: Live shellfish (clams, mussels) are bought for the day, or factory-frozen: live, they do not last the week. On Sunday just have the base ready.
ui.prHornoHuevo: Have the base of the recipe (sauce, vegetables, ham) divided into the ramekins, covered, in the fridge.
ui.prDHornoHuevo: Crack the eggs over the base and bake at 190 °C until the whites set and the yolks are still soft: about twelve minutes.
ui.prDNapolitana: Top with the sauce, ham and mozzarella, and broil five minutes.
ui.prEMigasD: Cut the bread and dampen it with salted water as the recipe says; cut the pork belly, chorizo and pepper, and peel the garlic.
ui.prEMigasA: Fry the pork belly and chorizo and, in that fat, the bread with the garlic, stirring nonstop until loose and golden: fifteen minutes. A fried egg on the side.
ui.prETorrijasD: Infuse the milk with cinnamon and peel, and slice the bread; the syrup or honey, in a jar.
ui.prETorrijasA: Soak the bread in the cold milk, dip it in egg and fry two minutes per side; sugar and cinnamon or honey on top.
ui.prDWantan: Bring the broth to a boil and cook the filled pasta (wontons or tortellini) in it from frozen, six minutes; leafy greens for the last minute.
ui.prFideoSeco: Toast the noodles in oil until golden and have the base ready with the stock (or the sofrito with the fumet). Toasted noodles and base, separate, in the fridge.
ui.prDFideoSeco: Bring the base to a boil, add the toasted noodles (and the seafood, if any) and cook covered about eight minutes, until they drink up the stock.
ui.prHornoVeg: Roast them through on Sunday and store: cold they keep four days and taste better on the second.
ui.prDHornoVeg: Serve them cold, or warm them five minutes in a pan or air fryer.
ui.prPapaAsada: Cut them as the recipe asks, par-boil six minutes in salted water, dry, toss in oil and freeze on a tray: the crisping happens on the day.
ui.prDPapaAsada: Straight from the freezer into the air fryer or a 220 °C oven, about 15 minutes, until golden.
ui.prFrio: Make it in full and keep it cold in jars or one-day containers. It is served cold, so there is nothing to reheat.
ui.prDFrio: Serve it cold; whatever goes on top (oil, herbs, egg, crunchy bits) goes on at the last moment.
ui.prArmado: Have the components ready and portioned: the filling or meat cooked, the sauce made, the cheese grated, the vegetables cut.
ui.prDArmado: Warm the sauce and filling, assemble with what is ready and give it a last blast of heat: ten minutes.
ui.prDTorta: Brown them from frozen in a pan with a little oil, five minutes per side (or air fryer at 200 °C, 12 minutes).
ui.prDGyoza: In an oiled pan, from frozen: brown two minutes, add a splash of water and cover six minutes.
ui.prDMasaHervida: Cook from frozen in boiling water or steam, six to eight minutes.
ui.prDPastaSalteada: Sauté the protein and the pre-cut vegetables as the recipe says (five minutes), dip the par-cooked pasta 60 seconds in boiling water and toss it all in the pan with a splash of that water.
ui.prFrito2: Marinate, coat and fry it through; drain on a rack, cool and freeze on a tray. That is how fried-chicken and Chinese restaurants work. The sauce, if any, in a jar.
ui.prDFrito2: Bring back the crust from frozen: air fryer at 200 °C or very hot oil, seven or eight minutes. If there is a sauce, warm it separately and toss at the last second.
ui.prTempura: Cut and dry the vegetables (or press and cut the tofu) and store in paper-lined containers. The dry batter mix, in a jar.
ui.prDTempura: Whisk the batter with ice water right then (one minute, lumps are fine), dip the pieces and fry in batches, six or seven minutes.
ui.prMachacado: Cook or par-fry the plantain (or cassava) and the protein as the recipe says, without mashing; cool and store by portion.
ui.prDMachacado: Heat the plantain or cassava in the pan with the fat and mash it hot with the garlic and the protein: ten minutes. Mashed cold, it will not bind.
ui.prSalsaLicuada: Blend the sauce on Sunday and keep it in a jar: three days. If it thickens, a splash of milk when serving.
ui.prDHuevoEnc: The egg is made on the day, at the last step, as the recipe says: four minutes.
ui.prEBandejaD1: Stewed beans, hogao, rice and ground beef browned with cumin: all four ready and portioned. The beans and the hogao are better the next day.
ui.prEBandejaD2: Pork belly pre-cooked in salted water until the water evaporates, without frying it yet; cool and store. On the day it just fries in its own fat.
ui.prEBandejaA1: Reheat the beans and rice covered. Meanwhile, in one pan, fry the pre-cooked pork belly until it puffs and, in its fat, the chorizos and the ground beef.
ui.prEBandejaA2: In the same fat, the ripe plantain and the eggs; the arepa in the toaster and the avocado cut when serving.
ui.prEMisoD: Make the dashi (the stock with bonito and ginger, strained), cut the carrot, mushroom and scallion, and keep the diced tofu covered in water in the fridge.
ui.prEMisoA: Heat the dashi with the carrot and mushroom five minutes, add the tofu and spinach two minutes, turn off the heat and dissolve the miso. It does not boil again.
ui.prEArepaHuevoD: Make the dough and give the arepas their first fry until they puff; cool and freeze them separately.
ui.prEArepaHuevoA: Leave them out of the freezer ten minutes, cut the slit, slip in the egg, seal and give them the second fry: four minutes each.
ui.prEAborrajadoD: Fry the ripe plantain, flatten it and build the sandwiches with cheese and guava paste; freeze them separately. The batter is not made ahead.
ui.prEAborrajadoA: Whisk the batter (two minutes), dip the aborrajados from frozen and fry over medium heat, six minutes.
ui.prEChilesD: Roast, peel, seed and stuff the chiles; keep them dry in the fridge. The broth, made and portioned.
ui.prEChilesA: Whip the whites to stiff peaks and fold in the yolks (three minutes), flour, coat and fry the chiles (eight minutes) and serve them over the hot broth.
ui.prESolomilloD: Cut into medallions, pat dry and portion; the garlic peeled and the fries par-cooked and frozen.
ui.prESolomilloA: Sear the medallions (four minutes), brown the garlic, add the whisky, lemon and stock, reduce and mount with cold butter: twelve minutes, with the fries in the air fryer at the same time.

raiz_dura.como: Boil 20–40 min, roast 40–60 min, or double-fry. Raw only grated or sliced thin.
raiz_dura.ojo: Cassava and yam will not yield to high, fast heat: they need water and time or they stay raw inside.

cruciferas.como: Steam 4–6 min, hard sauté 5–7 min, roast 18–25 min.
cruciferas.ojo: Overcooked they turn sulphurous and bitter. Keep them short and bright.

hoja_tierna.como: Seconds. Raw, or high heat just until they collapse.
hoja_tierna.ojo: In stews they go in at the end, off the heat: residual warmth cooks them.

aromatica_base.como: Sweat 5–10 min over medium heat until translucent; never brown the garlic before the onion.
aromatica_base.ojo: This is the base of most of the book. Burn it and the whole dish tastes bitter.

acuosa_tierna.como: 3–8 min over high heat in a wide pan, or roasted 15–20 min.
acuosa_tierna.ojo: They release water. In a crowded or lukewarm pan they stew in their own juice instead of browning.

hongos.como: Hot dry pan, not crowded, 5–8 min. Salt at the end.
hongos.ojo: Early salt draws out their water and boils them. They should sizzle, not bubble.

flor_fibrosa.como: Boil 30–45 min or braise. A whole artichoke asks for time.
flor_fibrosa.ojo: They oxidise once cut: hold them in water with lemon.

legumbre_seca.como: Soak 8 h, then simmer gently 45–90 min. Lentils need no soak: 25–30 min.
legumbre_seca.ojo: Salt and acid at the end. Added early, the bean never softens.

grano_cereal.como: Rice 15–18 min, quinoa 15 min, couscous 5 min resting, barley 40 min.
grano_cereal.ojo: Each grain has its own water ratio. Measuring beats improvising.

fruta_cocina.como: Ripe plantain 10–15 min; apple and pear 15–20 min; citrus only at the end.
fruta_cocina.ojo: Fruit sugar burns fast: medium heat, and do not walk away.

temp.pollo: In the thickest part, clear of the bone. Breast is best at 74–76 °C; thigh and leg take 77–82 °C and come out looser.
temp.pavo: Same minimum as chicken. Rest 10 minutes before carving.
temp.carne_molida: All ground meat goes to 71 °C: grinding puts the outside on the inside.
temp.carne_res: 63 °C plus a 3-minute rest is the safe minimum for a whole cut. The grades below are what gets ordered at the table.
temp.cordero: Served like beef. Past 71 °C it loses the fat that makes it lamb.
temp.cerdo: No need to take it to 71 °C any more. At 63 °C with a rest it stays juicy and safe.
temp.pescado: It should flake apart under a fork.
temp.camaron: Firm and opaque. One minute more and they turn to rubber.
temp.huevo: For fully cooked preparations: white and yolk both set.

solomillo: 3–4 min per side on a 3 cm medallion

pasos: Receiving and chilling
At 4 °C or below, kept away from anything eaten without cooking.
Do not wash it
Rinsing raw chicken sprays bacteria across the whole bench. It does not get washed.
Its own board and knife
Reserved for raw only. Never the same ones used for vegetables or cooked food.
Cleaning the bird
Remove packaging, excess fat and feathers with clean tools. If it needs drying, disposable paper; never soap.
Hands and surfaces
Wash before and after. Disinfect bench, board, knives and containers when you finish.
Cooking
74 °C at the centre, checked with a thermometer.
Receiving and chilling
Between 0 and 4 °C, on ice. Check the cold chain on arrival.
Freshness check

ca1.montaje: Brushed onto the protein in the last minutes on the grill, in two or three coats.
ca1.porque: It covers all three savoury axes at once: salt and umami from the soy, explosive acidity from the passion fruit, molasses sweetness from the panela. No fat, which is why it glazes rather than sauces: the fire on the protein supplies what is missing. Early on, the panela burns.

comp.como: Reduce the soy with the panela over medium heat until it threads. Off the heat, strained passion fruit juice, grated ginger and garlic. Back on the heat for two minutes, never at a hard boil.

ca2.n: Beef with passion fruit teriyaki and blue cheese sauce
ca2.montaje: The two sauces are made separately and poured over the same piece of meat on the plate, never stirred together: one on each side, or in a zigzag.
ca2.porque: Two opposing sauces that meet in the mouth and not in the pan. The blue cheese brings fat and a fermented salt that runs deeper than soy; the teriyaki brings the acid that cuts that richness. Combined in one pan they would cancel each other out — kept apart, each bite can lean one way or the other.

comp.como: The same as above: soy and panela reduced, passion fruit off the heat.
Melt the cheese into the cream over low heat, stirring, until it binds. Finish with cold butter off the heat and freshly ground pepper.

ca3.montaje: Rub it over the protein and marinate at least four hours, covered and cold.
ca3.porque: Ají panca is colour and dried fruit, almost no heat, so it does not fight the meat. The vinegar is the vehicle: it opens the fibre and carries the garlic and cumin inward, which an oil-based marinade never manages. Dried oregano survives the hours without turning bitter.

comp.como: Blend the ají panca paste with the vinegar, garlic, cumin and oregano until smooth.

ca4.montaje: Served on the side, in a sauce boat, or spooned under whatever goes on top.
ca4.porque: The mustard does two jobs: volatile heat, and stabilising the emulsion, because its mucilage holds the fat. Raw garlic gives the edge mayonnaise alone lacks. Grated, not chopped, or it stays in pieces.

comp.como: Grate the garlic fine and work it into the mayonnaise with the mustard and a few drops of lemon until smooth.

ca5.n: The universal base: oil, garlic and lemon
ca5.montaje: Poured over fish, shellfish or vegetables straight off the heat.
ca5.porque: The full tripod in three things: fat, aromatic and acid. It works in any cuisine because it contributes structure rather than a dominant flavour. When a dish tastes flat, it is usually missing one of these three, not some new ingredient.

comp.como: Heat the oil with sliced garlic from cold, over medium heat, until barely golden. Off the heat, lemon juice and zest.

ca6.montaje: At the end the meat comes out and the liquid is reduced until it naps; poured over at the table.
ca6.porque: Panela on its own cloys. The bitterness of the beer and the heat of the mustard rein it in from two different sides, and the dark stock supplies the depth none of the three have. Barbecue logic, with molasses instead of refined sugar.

comp.como: Sear the meat, lift it out and deglaze with the beer. Add the dark stock, the panela and the mustard, return the meat and braise covered until it yields.

ca7.montaje: Marinate two to four hours and cook over high heat, short, draining well before it hits the pan.
ca7.porque: Sesame oil is perfume, not a cooking medium: toasted and volatile, it burns if you fry in it. Vinegar and soy carry; ginger and garlic perfume; the pepper brings vegetal sweetness and body.

comp.como: Mix the soy and vinegar with grated ginger and garlic and finely diced pepper. The sesame oil last, off the heat.

ca8.n: Cream cheese, lemon and soy spread
ca8.montaje: For canapés, as a cold sauce for fish, or as a filling for rolls.
ca8.porque: The boldest of yours and the one that best explains your cooking. Soy in a dairy base is uncommon, and that is the point: it gives cream cheese a savoury depth it lacks alone, and the lemon keeps it from turning heavy.

comp.como: Work the cream cheese at room temperature with the soy and the juice and zest of lemon until smooth. Chives at the end.

ca9.n: Vegetables with tahini, balsamic and pineapple
ca9.montaje: The tahini sauce goes down first, the roast vegetables and pineapple on top, and the reduction drizzled last.
ca9.porque: Each element supplies what the other two lack: tahini brings fat and a sesame bitterness, the balsamic concentrated sweetness and acid, the pineapple freshness and enzymes. Mixed in one bowl the pineapple would water down the tahini and the reduction would be lost; kept apart, each one registers.

comp.como: Whisk the tahini with lemon juice and grated garlic. Add ice water little by little: it seizes and thickens first, then loosens into a cream.
Reduce the balsamic with a touch of panela over low heat until it threads on the spoon.
Thick rings, lightly oiled, marked on a hot grill or pan until they caramelise on both sides. Coarse salt as they come off.

desinfeccion.sub: Order matters: soil first, disinfection second. Put dirty produce straight into chlorine and the organic matter consumes it, leaving the solution useless.
pasos: Wash under running water
Under the tap, scrubbing, until no soil is left. This step removes most of the dirt; the chlorine only finishes the job.
Make up the solution
At room temperature. Cold lowers chlorine efficacy, so do not use iced water.
Soak for 3 to 5 minutes
Fully submerged. Less is not enough and more adds nothing.
Rinse with drinking water
Under clean running water, so no taste or chlorine residue is left.
Change the solution
As produce goes in, the chlorine is used up. Do not keep it beyond 24 hours, and change it sooner if the water looks cloudy.
desinfeccion.calcSub: It depends on the strength of the bleach you buy, which is on the label. Enter the litres of water in your tub and the percentage on the bottle.
ojo: Never mix bleach with ammonia or cleaners containing it: it forms chloramine, a toxic gas.

Vinegar with baking soda, the formula that circulates most, does not disinfect: they are an acid and a base that neutralise each other. Vinegar alone helps a little and baking soda helps lift pesticide residue, but neither replaces chlorine against bacteria.
More chlorine is not better. Overdoing it leaves a taste, damages the produce and kills no more.
desinfeccion.fuente: Concentrations from the OIRSA guide on chlorine use in food establishments, following the FAO manual: 50 ppm for fruit and 100 ppm for vegetables, 3 to 5 minutes.

calor.sub: The temperature at the center of the piece, taken with a thermometer, is the only test that counts. Color lies.
temps: Chicken, turkey, duck, ground poultry and anything stuffed with them, at the thickest part.
Ground beef or pork: burgers, meatballs, fillings. Grinding puts the outside on the inside.
Whole cuts of beef, pork, lamb
Steaks, chops and roasts, with a three-minute rest before cutting.
Or until the flesh is opaque and flakes. Anything eaten raw comes from a suitable supplier and stays very cold.
Until it steams at the center, not lukewarm. Reheat only once: whatever is left after reheating gets thrown out.
calor.peligro: Bacteria multiply fast there. Cooked food spends no more than two hours at room temperature; less in hot weather.
pasos: Cool in two stages
From 60 to 21 °C within two hours, and from 21 to 5 °C in the next four. A big pot does not cool by itself in the fridge: the center stays warm for hours.
Divide and spread
Use shallow containers, spread rice on a tray, and if needed set the pot in an ice-water bath, stirring.
Cover when cold
Let the steam out uncovered and cover once it is no longer hot. Into the fridge within two hours.
Thaw in the fridge
Overnight, never on the counter. Thawed raw food gets cooked and is not refrozen raw.
Label
What it is and the date. Cooked food: three to four days in the fridge. Whatever will not be eaten by then goes to the freezer the same day.
calor.fuente: Internal temperatures per USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS); two-stage cooling per the FDA Food Code.
